$comment: Cross-SDK disagreements that are known, understood, and being worked. Every entry needs a reason and a hard expiry. NEW drift fails the run; an expired entry fails the run; and a recorded entry whose SDKs now AGREE also fails, because a note describing a state that no longer exists is the same rot as a stale finding. Baseline taken 2026-08-13 from the first three-SDK run (python, go, typescript). Nothing here is acceptable — it is the work list. 2026-08-13 later the same day: nine entries removed after the TypeScript int8 coercion, pathIn decode and datalog arity fixes landed — the runner refuses to keep an entry whose SDKs now agree. 2026-08-13, third pass: the four SQL/vector entries removed after the engine fixes landed — dimensionless-VECTOR row omission and the statement-Describe column typing. The three that remain are SDK-side work, not engine defects. 2026-08-15: elixir joined the matrix once the engine gained ARRAY(subquery) and correct irregular pg_type I/O names, taking it from 42/42 failing at connect to 32 pass / 0 fail. Its arrival surfaced five NEW disagreements, every one an Elixir SDK method that does not exist rather than an engine defect — they were invisible while the SDK could not connect at all. 2026-08-15 later: all five elixir entries removed the same day they were added — the missing SDK surface was implemented rather than left recorded. The runner forced this: it fails an entry whose SDKs now agree, so a note describing a state that no longer exists cannot survive a run. 2026-08-15: cdc.read_returns_a_list removed — Go and Rust now decode CDC events into a typed list like Python and TypeScript. The note was half stale when read: TypeScript had already been parsing correctly. Two Go unit tests asserted only `result != ""`, which any non-empty payload satisfies — the exact truthy-string false green the entry warned about, sitting inside the tests meant to catch it. 2026-08-15: document.get_path_returns_a_decoded_scalar removed — Go now returns the decoded value, which needed the *string -> any signature break S22 flagged and nobody had taken. TypeScript turned out to have been decoding already, so half that entry was stale when read. One entry remains: timeseries.range_query, which is a contract question (three SDKs, three answers) rather than a port that was never done. 2026-08-15: timeseries.range_query removed, and with it the LAST entry — the file is empty for the first time. It was the one entry that was a contract question rather than a missing port: raw point retrieval had no SQL surface at all, so Python synthesised it from sixty bucketed TS_RANGE_AVG calls (sixty round trips for points the store already held, and lossy wherever a bucket held more than one), Go refused, and TypeScript threw. Settled at the right layer by adding TS_RANGE to the engine rather than picking one of the three client behaviours. All five SDKs now answer identically.
